stem: One drying zone is progressing much faster than another even though the room's nominal setpoints are the same. What should be checked first?
choices: Local airflow, temperature, humidity, loading density, and representative sampling in each zone.
Harvest-date differences between the zones, because elapsed time is usually the strongest explanation when setpoints match.
Preharvest plant height and canopy position, because those factors are generally more important than local drying-zone conditions.
The room-controller setpoints again, because matching programmed values usually means the drying environment is spatially uniform.
rationale: Local environmental conditions and loading can differ within a room. Mapping those differences helps explain uneven drying.
